title: Haunted ship tour returns with cryptid theme, new 'lights on' option
excerpt: The Deck’s haunted ship tour this October features the Captain’s Curse, a mystery theme centered on cryptids aboard the Irvin freighter
content:
DULUTH, Minn. (Northern News Now) The DECC’s haunted ship tour this October features the Captain’s Curse, a mystery theme centered on cryptids aboard the William A. Irvin.

The attraction starts outside the ship with sea-life tendrils reaching up the sides of the vessel, described as now captain-less. The experience continues the length of the 610-foot ship, with crew members portraying various cryptids throughout the ship’s nooks and crannies.

Cryptid theme and effects

DECC leaders say the ship focuses on cryptids, creatures that are part of myth and lore but cannot be confirmed to exist. The tour uses actors as well as mechanical props obtained from the National Haunting Tour.

Amundsen said audio, lighting and a simulated thunderstorm on the ship are layered together to build the atmosphere experienced during the tour.

The DECC is introducing the Lights On Tour this year for guests who want to view the attraction’s artistic and visual elements without jump scares, Amundsen said. She described the tour as gory and said it is not intended for 6-year-olds, but added that many 10-year-olds enjoy it.

The Lights On Tour will run on the afternoons of Saturday, Oct. 3, and Saturday, Oct. 10, from 1 p.m. to 3 p.m. It includes strewn lights, bonfires, and food and drinks available for purchase.

Hours, pricing and other details

The season began Friday, Oct. 2, and runs Thursdays, Fridays and Saturdays through Halloween.

Amundsen said Thursdays have fewer guests and are promoted as a discount, “locals night,” with tickets $5 off.

Ticket prices are $25 on Fridays and Saturdays, discounts are available for military members and college students. The Lights On Tour costs less than the regular tour, Amundsen said.

The DECC advises that no child under 12 will be admitted without a parent, and parental guidance is suggested. Due to the historic nature of the ship, the tour is not handicapped accessible.
